description: plain-features with AES-256 (R6) and the non-ASCII user password 'pässwörd' (owner 'owner'). R6 passwords are UTF-8 after SASLprep, so a reader must encode the typed password as UTF-8 to open it.

Invalid combination: %PDF-1.7 with AES-256 (R6) encryption, empty user password, owner 'owner', but no /Extensions ADBE (BaseVersion 1.7, ExtensionLevel 8) in the catalog. R6 is not part of plain PDF 1.7, so validators should flag the missing declaration or want the header raised to 2.0. The generator blanks the extension qpdf writes, keeping all offsets.

Invalid combination: %PDF-2.0 encrypted with 128-bit RC4 (Standard handler R3), user password 'user', owner 'owner'. PDF 2.0 deprecates RC4 and allows only R6 (AES-256), so validators should flag it. Readers may still open it with the password.

Two-page %PDF-2.0 file with a Link annotation on page 1 going to page 2 (Fit) and a Text (note) annotation with Contents 'note'. Page tools must keep the link pointing at the right page and keep the note.

%PDF-2.0 with object and cross-reference streams. Title only in XMP (dc:title 'XMP Title 2.0'), Info holds only CreationDate. The bookmark title is a UTF-8 text string (BOM EF BB BF) that must decode as 'UTF8 été ✓', not as PDFDocEncoding. Catalog /AF lists an embedded data.csv with AFRelationship /Data, and page 1 has its own OutputIntents. After a rewrite the header must stay %PDF-2.0 and the AF, the UTF-8 title and the page OutputIntents must survive.

description: Regression: cert-sign on an AES-256 (R6) owner-restricted 2.0 file appended an incremental update with plain-text objects and a cross-reference stream without /Encrypt. qpdf then reads the encrypted object stream as plain Flate and stops with 'unable to find page tree'; PDFium still finds three pages. A fixed signer must keep the file openable by qpdf, or refuse without the owner password.

rich-features with AES-256 (R6), empty user password, owner password 'owner', and EncryptMetadata false, so the XMP stream stays plain text while everything else is encrypted. Readers must not try to decrypt the metadata stream, and a re-save must keep EncryptMetadata false.

rich-features encrypted with AES-256 (R6), empty user password, owner password 'owner'. Modify, extract and high-resolution print are refused (P -3100). Opens without a password; anything that rewrites it must keep R6 and the permissions, or say it needs the owner password.
rich-features with AES-256 (R6), user password 'user' and owner password 'owner'. Without a password it must be refused as encrypted, not reported as damaged.

PDF 2.0 features in one file: a structure tree in the PDF 2.0 namespace (http://iso.org/pdf2/ssn, /Namespaces on the root, DocumentFragment, P and Aside), DPartRoot document parts over all three pages, ExtGState UseBlackPtComp, page and catalog /AF with AFRelationship /Source and the Unicode UF 'sóurce-数据.xml', Projection and RichMedia annotations, page OutputIntents and /Lang en-GB. Tools should keep these keys, not drop them as unknown, and leave the header at %PDF-2.0.
